info.title: Ask O11y - AI-Powered Observability Assistant API
info.description:
REST API for Ask O11y Grafana plugin. Provides AI-powered observability assistance through natural language conversations. Users can query metrics, logs, traces, manage dashboards, and troubleshoot issues without writing PromQL/LogQL or navigating complex UIs.

## Authentication
All endpoints (except `/health` and `/`) require Grafana session authentication via the `grafana_session` cookie.

## Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
The plugin enforces role-based access control:
- **Admin/Editor**: Full access to all endpoints and MCP tools
- **Viewer**: Read-only access (MCP tools with `readOnlyHint: true` annotation only)

## Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
All endpoints support multi-tenant organization isolation via headers:
- `X-Grafana-Org-Id`: Numeric organization ID (defaults to "1")
- `X-Scope-OrgID`: Tenant name (optional)
- Sessions, shares, and agent runs are scoped to user + organization

## Rate Limiting
- Session sharing: 50 shares per hour per user

## Limits
- Max sessions per user/org: 50 (oldest auto-evicted)
- Max agent iterations per run: 25
- Max events per run: 500
- Default token limit: 128,000

get.description: Returns the health status of the plugin and MCP server connectivity. This endpoint does not require authentication.
Informational endpoint that returns plugin metadata. This endpoint does not require authentication.
Returns the complete OpenAPI 3.0.3 specification for this API. This endpoint does not require authentication.

post.description: Raw MCP protocol JSON-RPC 2.0 proxy endpoint. Forwards requests to configured MCP servers. This is a low-level endpoint; most users should use `/api/mcp/tools` and `/api/mcp/call-tool` instead.

get.description: Returns a list of available MCP tools filtered by the user's role. Admin/Editor roles see all tools, while Viewer role only sees tools with `readOnlyHint: true` annotation. Tools from multiple MCP servers are aggregated.

post.description: Executes an MCP tool with RBAC enforcement. The tool must be available in the user's filtered tool list (see `/api/mcp/tools`). Admin/Editor roles can access all tools, while Viewer role can only access tools with `readOnlyHint: true` annotation. RBAC is enforced both at tool listing time and at execution time (double-check pattern).

example.error: Access denied: Viewer role cannot access tool create_dashboard

get.description: Returns health status for all configured MCP servers. Used for monitoring MCP server connectivity.

oauth.description: Per-user OAuth connection state keyed by server ID; present only for servers configured with an oauth block.

post.description:
Starts an agentic conversation loop in detached mode. The agent processes the user's message asynchronously, calling MCP tools as needed. Returns immediately with a `runId` and `sessionId`. Use `/api/agent/runs/{runId}/events` to stream the results via SSE.

## RBAC
Tool execution within the agent loop respects user role permissions. Viewer role can only use read-only tools.

## Iteration Limit
Max 25 iterations per run.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Optional explicit LLM app model abstraction to use for this session. Omit to let Ask O11y choose base or large from the task type and message complexity. Once explicitly set on a session, later runs must use the same model.

model.description: Effective model selected for this run

modelSource.description: How the effective model was chosen

get.summary: Get agent run status and events
get.description: Returns the current status and all events for an agent run. Only the user who created the run (in the same organization) can access it.

example.error: Access denied: run belongs to different user or org

get.description:
Streams all events for an agent run using Server-Sent Events (SSE). Replays all historical events, then streams new events until the run completes. Includes keepalive comments every 15 seconds. Only the user who created the run (in the same organization) can access it.

This endpoint is useful for reconnecting to an in-progress run after a page refresh.

schema.description: SSE stream replaying all historical events, then streaming new events until completion

post.description: Cancels a running agent. Only the user who created the run (in the same organization) can cancel it. Returns 409 if the run is not currently running.

409.description: Run is not running (already completed, failed, or cancelled)

example.error: Run is not in running state

post.description: Approves or rejects a pending approval-gated tool call for an agent run. Duplicate same-decision requests are idempotent.

200.description: Eval capture state and captured eval rows

get.summary: Get Graphiti-backed topology for agent Scenes

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Optional topology search query sent to Graphiti memory.

parameters.name: maxNodes
parameters.description: Maximum service nodes to return. Defaults to 100 and is capped server-side.

parameters.name: maxEdges
parameters.description: Maximum graph edges to return. Defaults to 200 and is capped server-side.

get.description: Returns the built-in default prompt templates from the Go backend. Used by the frontend settings UI to populate prompt editors and power the 'Reset to Default' button. The Go backend is the single source of truth for prompt defaults.

405.description: Method not allowed (only GET is supported)

get.description: Returns a list of all sessions for the current user in the current organization. Sessions are sorted by last update time (most recent first). Max 50 sessions per user/org; oldest sessions are auto-evicted when limit is reached.

post.description: Creates a new chat session. If this is the first session for the user/org, it is automatically set as the current session. Max 50 sessions per user/org; oldest sessions are auto-evicted when limit is reached.

title.description: Session title (auto-generated from first message if not provided)

delete.description: Deletes all sessions for the current user in the current organization. This action is irreversible.

get.description: Returns the ID of the current active session for the user/org, or empty string if no current session is set.

sessionId.description: Current session ID (empty string if none)

put.description: Sets the specified session as the current active session for the user/org. Pass empty string to clear the current session.

sessionId.description: Session ID to set as current (empty string to clear)

delete.description: Clears the current active session for the user/org. Equivalent to PUT with empty sessionId.

get.description: Returns full session details including all messages. Only the session owner (same user + org) can access it.

put.description: Updates session metadata (title, summary) or appends messages. Only the session owner (same user + org) can update it.

delete.description: Deletes a session. Only the session owner (same user + org) can delete it. This action is irreversible.

get.description: Returns all active shares created by the current user for the specified session.

Returns cumulative usage stats (tokens, turns, tool calls) for a session, accumulated across all its agent runs. Only the session owner (same user + org) can access it. Omits the full message history — use GET /api/sessions/{sessionId} for the full transcript.

post.description: Creates a shareable link for a session snapshot. The share is scoped to the organization and can be accessed by any user in the same org. Rate limited to 50 shares per hour per user. The share contains a snapshot of the session at creation time (not live updates).

sessionData.description: Full session object (must include id and messages fields)

expiresInDays.description: Expiration time in days (optional, converted to hours)

shareId.description: Cryptographically secure share ID (base64 URL-safe 32-byte token)

shareUrl.description: Full URL to access the shared session

get.description: Returns a read-only snapshot of a shared session. The share must belong to the same organization as the requesting user. The returned session includes `isShared: true` and `sharedBy` fields.

sharedBy.description: User ID who created the share

403.description: Access denied (not in same org as share)

example.error: Share not found or access denied

delete.description: Revokes a share link. Only the user who created the share can revoke it. After revocation, the share URL will no longer be accessible.

403.description: Access denied (user doesn't own this share)

example.error: You do not have permission to delete this share

get.description: Returns the knowledge graph connection status, including whether the Graphiti integration is enabled and currently connected.

enabled.description: Whether the knowledge graph client is configured

connected.description: Whether the knowledge graph service is reachable

post.description: Starts a background discovery agent session that explores the full observability environment and ingests findings into the knowledge graph. Returns immediately with a run ID that can be polled for status.

runId.description: Unique run ID for tracking the discovery session

status.description: Initial status of the discovery run

post.description: Ingests conversation messages from a completed investigation session into the knowledge graph. This is the 'Feed to Knowledge Graph' action — the user opts in to share their investigation findings so future sessions can leverage discovered causal relationships (e.g., 'service A failed because database B connection pool was exhausted').

400.description: Invalid request or knowledge graph not configured

get.description: Begins the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow (with PKCE when configured) for the current Grafana user against an OAuth-enabled MCP server. Responds with a 302 redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint. Intended to be opened in a popup window.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint

404.description: Server unknown or has no OAuth configuration

get.description: Redirect target registered with the authorization server. Validates the one-shot state, exchanges the code for tokens, persists them for the initiating user, and returns a small HTML page that notifies the opener window via postMessage and closes itself.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code issued by the provider

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Provider error code when the grant was denied

200.description: HTML page reporting the outcome to the opener window

get.description: Reports whether the current Grafana user has connected their account for an OAuth-enabled MCP server.

404.description: Server unknown or has no OAuth configuration

post.description: Deletes the current Grafana user's stored token for an OAuth-enabled MCP server.

404.description: Server unknown or has no OAuth configuration

get.description: Returns the built-in catalog of one-click external MCP providers (GitHub read-only, GitHub read/write, Atlassian) so the admin UI can render preset cards.
Returns MCP servers added at runtime through the admin UI. OAuth client credentials are never included in responses.

post.summary: Provision an MCP server from a preset
post.description: Admin-only. Attaches a preset external MCP server. For DCR-capable providers (Atlassian) OAuth endpoints are discovered via RFC 8414/9728 and a client is registered via RFC 7591 automatically; for others (GitHub) the admin supplies clientId and optionally clientSecret.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID; required for presets without dynamic client registration

403.description: Caller is not a Grafana Admin

502.description: OAuth discovery or dynamic client registration against the provider failed

post.summary: Provision a generic OAuth-gated MCP server
post.description: Admin-only. Attaches any MCP server that authenticates users via OAuth 2.0 authorization-code. With discover=true the OAuth endpoints (and client registration when clientId is empty) are resolved automatically from the server's advertised metadata.

discover.description: Resolve OAuth endpoints (and register a client when clientId is empty) from the server's advertised metadata

403.description: Caller is not a Grafana Admin

502.description: OAuth discovery or dynamic client registration against the provider failed

delete.summary: Remove a dynamically provisioned MCP server
delete.description: Admin-only. Detaches the server from the MCP proxy and deletes its persisted record and OAuth configuration.

403.description: Caller is not a Grafana Admin
